# Thirza Abernethy

## Overview

- **Age:** Over sixty  <sub>[v1 c1 P23](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0023), [v1 c9 P44](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0044)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013)</sub>
- **Status:** Unmarried  <sub>[v1 c6 P34](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0034)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley, St. Brendan’s Island  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P7](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0007)</sub>
- **Role:** Homemaker and farm manager  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c4 P40](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0040), [v1 c6 P29](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0029)</sub>

## Appearance

Thirza is a tall, slender woman with sharp angles rather than curves. She has dark hair streaked with gray, which she constantly binds at the back in a tight, firm bun held combatively with wire hairpins. Her face has a stern expression, though a redeeming, humorous twitch sometimes touches her lips.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 c1 P15](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0015)_

## Personality

Thirza gives the impression of having a limited background and an unyielding sense of morality, though she possesses a redeeming sense of humor. She is an outstanding homemaker who keeps her house agonizingly clean and orderly, highly valuing tidiness and practical discipline. Though she is often sharp, abrupt, and strict with children, she harbors a deep, unspoken capacity for affection, compassion, and moral duty.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009), [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 c4 P10](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0010), [v1 c5 P21](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0021), [v1 c7 P1](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0001), [v1 c7 P19](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0019), [v1 c10 P50](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0050)_

## History

Thirza Abernethy resides at Grey Shutters with her brother Obed. Having agreed to adopt a young orphan boy to assist on the farm, they are shocked when Obed returns from the station with an eleven-year-old girl named Nell Harcourt instead. Although Thirza initially insists on returning Nell to the asylum, she accompanies Nell to Pale Sands to make arrangements. Upon seeing the woman who might otherwise take Nell, Thirza refuses to surrender the orphan and agrees to keep her at Grey Shutters, taking on the responsibility of raising her. She instructs Nell in homemaking, proper behavior, and religious prayers, attempting to curb the girl's wild imagination and loquacity. When neighbor Agatha Sowerby insults Nell's appearance, causing Nell to fly into a rage, Thirza insists Nell apologize, though she secretly defends Nell's feelings to Agatha. Later, Thirza wrongly accuses Nell of stealing and losing her cherished amethyst brooch, locking Nell in her room until she falsely confesses, only for Thirza to discover the brooch tangled in her own shawl. Over time, Thirza grows deeply attached to Nell, eventually admitting that the girl has brought her a new sense of motherhood and happiness. When Nell refuses to return to school after being humiliated by her teacher, Thirza, on Agatha's advice, allows her to study at home instead. She later supports Nell through her various mishaps, including the accidental intoxication of her friend Isolde with homemade currant wine.

## Background by volume

- Grew up in Brierley in the house built by her father  <sub>[v1 c1 P6](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0006), [v1 c1 P31](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0031)</sub>

## Quotes

> Agatha, it was wrong of you to mock her appearance.  <sub>[v1 c9 P26](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0026)</sub>

> I disbelieve in using names for people that do not belong to them.  <sub>[v1 c8 P13](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0013)</sub>

> Nell, your age is sufficient for you to offer your own prayers. Simply express gratitude to God for what He has bestowed upon you, and modestly request from Him the items you desire.  <sub>[v1 c7 P20](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0020)</sub>

> I have pondered the concept so long that I am somewhat accustomed to it. A duty of sorts is what it feels like. Raising a child, a girl in particular, is something I have never done, and I suppose I will fail miserably at it. Even so, my best effort will be given.  <sub>[v1 c6 P31](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0031)</sub>

> I am not asking you to picture it. Oh, I perceive that you dislike the attire! What is wrong with it? Are the garments not tidy, spotless, and brand-new?  <sub>[v1 c11 P4](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0004)</sub>
